The '''2021–22 season''' was [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal Football Club]]'s 30th season in the [[Premier League]], their [[List of Arsenal F.C. seasons|96th consecutive season]] in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of English football and 105th season in the top flight overall.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/features/48523/behind-the-numbers- |title=All-time Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=18 June 2013 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=22 June 2023 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622042610/https://www.arsenal.com/news/features/48523/behind-the-numbers- |archive-date=22 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engall.html |title=English Clubs Divisional Movements 1888–2016 |last1=Ross |first1=James |last2=Heneghan |first2=Michael |last3=Orford |first3=Stuart |last4=Culliton |first4=Eoin |date=25 August 2016 |publisher=[[RSSSF|Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]] |access-date=22 June 2023 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622041929/https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engall.html |archive-date=22 June 2023}}</ref> It began on 1 July 2021 and concluded on 30 June 2022, with competitive matches played between August and May. In addition to the [[2021–22 Premier League|domestic league]], Arsenal also participated in the [[2021–22 FA Cup|FA Cup]] and [[2021–22 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], but they did not participate in any European competition for the first time since [[1995–96 Arsenal F.C. season|1995–96]], owing to an eighth-place finish the [[2020–21 Premier League|previous season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/may/23/arsenal-brighton-premier-league-match-report|title=Arsenal miss out on Europe despite Nicolas Pépé double against Brighton|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=The Guardian|date=23 May 2021|access-date=23 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/tottenham-europa-conference-league-premier-league-results-2020-21-b936770.html|title=Tottenham seal Europa Conference League spot; Arsenal miss out on European football for first time in 25 years|first=Giuseppe|last=Muro|newspaper=[[Evening Standard]]|date=23 May 2021|access-date=4 June 2021}}</ref>

Managed by [[Mikel Arteta]] in his second full season, Arsenal were the youngest team in the Premier League with an average starting age of 24 years and 308 days – more than a whole year younger than the next team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/premier-league-stats-review-emirates-stadium-attendance-goals-appearances |title=Our 2021/22 season in numbers |last=James |first=Josh |date=23 May 2022 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=28 June 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/12611391/premier-league-top-trends-revealed-for-the-2021-22-season |title=Premier League: Top trends revealed for the 2021/22 season |last=Smith |first=Adam |date=24 May 2022 |publisher=Sky Sports |access-date=28 June 2022 }}</ref> They finished fifth in the Premier League, and qualified for next season's [[2022–23 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]].

The season was documented in the [[Amazon Prime Video]] series ''[[All or Nothing: Arsenal]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/amazon-prime-all-or-nothing-arsenal-release-dates-trailer |title=Watch the trailer for All or Nothing: Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=28 June 2022 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=30 June 2022 }}</ref>

== Overview ==
=== June and July ===
On 24 June, Greek centre-back [[Konstantinos Mavropanos]]'s loan spell at [[Bundesliga]] club [[VfB Stuttgart|Stuttgart]] was extended for another season.<ref name="dinos">{{cite news|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/dinos-mavropanos-rejoins-stuttgart-loan|title=Dinos Mavropanos rejoins Stuttgart on loan|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=24 June 2021|access-date=24 June 2021}}</ref>

[[File:David Luiz ConfedCup2013Champions17.jpg|thumb|right|200px|David Luiz playing for [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] in 2013]]

On 1 July, Arsenal released several players, of which the only first-team player was Brazilian centre-back [[David Luiz]], who was at the end of his contract; Luiz later joined Brazilian [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|top-flight]] side [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Flamengo]] in September.<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arteta-david-luiz-leaving-club|title=Arteta on... David Luiz leaving the club|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=18 May 2021|access-date=24 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/soccer-transfers/story/4472957/david-luiz-joins-brazilian-club-flamengo|title=David Luiz joins Brazilian club Flamengo|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=11 September 2021|access-date=25 October 2021}}</ref> At the same time, Spanish midfielder [[Dani Ceballos]] and Australian goalkeeper [[Mathew Ryan]] finished their loan spells<ref name="released">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/club-announces-released-players|title=Club announces released players|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=3 June 2021|access-date=3 June 2021}}</ref> and returned to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]], respectively, though the latter would join [[Real Sociedad]] on 12 July.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.brightonandhovenews.org/2021/07/12/top-spanish-club-sign-brighton-and-hove-albion-goalkeeper|title=Top Spanish club sign Brighton and Hove Albion goalkeeper|first=Frank|last=le Duc|publisher=Brighton and Hove News|date=12 July 2021|access-date=12 July 2021}}</ref> On 6 July, French midfielder [[Matteo Guendouzi]], who spent the entirety of the [[2020–21 Hertha BSC season|previous season]] on loan at [[Bundesliga]] club [[Hertha BSC|Hertha Berlin]], was once again loaned out, this time to [[Ligue 1]] club [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] for the entire [[2021–22 Ligue 1|Ligue 1 season]].<ref name="guendouzi">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/matteo-guendouzi-joins-marseille-loan|title=Matteo Guendouzi joins Marseille on loan|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=6 July 2021|access-date=6 July 2021}}</ref> Arsenal's first signing of the summer transfer window came on 10 July, with 21-year-old Portuguese left-back [[Nuno Tavares]] arriving from [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] for about £8&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/12352858/nuno-tavares-arsenal-sign-benfica-defender-in-first-summer-transfer-window-signing|title=Nuno Tavares: Arsenal sign Benfica defender in first summer transfer window signing|website=[[Sky Sports]]|date=10 July 2021|access-date=25 October 2021}}</ref><ref name="nuno" />

Arsenal had four players unavailable for pre-season friendlies, as [[Bernd Leno]], [[Bukayo Saka]], [[Kieran Tierney]], and [[Granit Xhaka]] had competed in [[UEFA Euro 2020|Euro 2020]], which ended on 11 July. On 13 July, Arsenal began their pre-season tour of Scotland with a 2–1 defeat to [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]. This was followed by a match four days later against defending [[2020–21 Scottish Premiership|Scottish champions]] [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], who were celebrating their 150th anniversary. Arsenal fell behind twice but recovered for a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2021-Jul-17/rangers-2-2-arsenal-match-report|title=Match report: Rangers 2-2 Arsenal|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=17 July 2021|access-date=25 October 2021}}</ref>

Between the two Scottish friendlies, it was announced on 15 July that French centre-back [[William Saliba]], who spent the second half of last season on loan at [[OGC Nice|Nice]], would join Guendouzi at Marseille on a season-long loan deal.<ref name="saliba">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/william-saliba-joins-marseille-loan|title=William Saliba joins Marseille on loan|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=15 July 2021|access-date=15 July 2021}}</ref> On 19 July, Arsenal made their second acquisition, signing 21-year-old Belgian midfielder [[Albert Sambi Lokonga]] from [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]] for about £17.2&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57893045|title=Arsenal sign Albert Sambi Lokonga from Anderlecht on long-term contract|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=19 July 2021|access-date=25 October 2021}}</ref><ref name="albert" />

The day after, Arsenal withdrew from the seventh edition of the [[Florida Cup (soccer)|Florida Cup]], citing "a small number of positive [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports|COVID-19]] tests" among the staff.<ref name="FloridaCupWithdrawal">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/us-trip-after-positive-covid-tests|title=US trip off after positive COVID tests|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=20 July 2021|access-date=21 July 2021}}</ref> They had been set to compete with fellow [[Premier League]] club [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], [[Serie A]] club [[Inter Milan]], and Colombian [[Categoría Primera A|top-flight]] club [[Millonarios F.C.|Millionarios]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57923967|title=Florida Cup: Arsenal & Inter Milan withdraw from tournament because of Covid-19 cases and risks|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=21 July 2021|access-date=25 October 2021}}</ref> but they and fellow withdrawals Inter Milan were replaced by [[Atlético Nacional]], also from the Colombian first division, and [[Liga MX]] club [[Club Universidad Nacional|Pumas UNAM]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.clickorlando.com/sports/2021/07/23/2-teams-added-to-orlandos-florida-cup/|title=2 teams added to Orlando's Florida Cup|first=Jon|last=Jankowski|website=ClickOrlando.com|publisher=[[WKMG-TV]]|date=23 July 2021|access-date=26 October 2021}}</ref>

In lieu of the Florida Cup matches, Arsenal organised friendlies at their [[Arsenal Training Centre|London Colney]] training ground against two other London sides, [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] from the [[EFL Championship]] on 24 July and newly promoted Premier League side [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] on 28 July, with both matches finishing 4–1 to Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2021-Jul-24/arsenal-4-1-millwall-match-report|title=Match report: Arsenal 4-1 Millwall|first=Max|last=Jones|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=24 July 2021|access-date=26 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2021-Jul-28/arsenal-4-1-watford-match-report|title=Match report: Arsenal 4-1 Watford|first=Max|last=Jones|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=28 July 2021|access-date=26 October 2021}}</ref>

Arsenal concluded the month with the announced signing of 23-year-old English centre-back [[Ben White (footballer)|Ben White]] on 30 July, who joined from fellow Premier League club [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] on a £50&nbsp;million deal.<ref name="ben-white" />

=== August ===
To finish their pre-season, Arsenal participated in the Mind Series pre-season tournament, which supported [[Mind (charity)|Mind]] and other mental health charities, against London rivals [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref name="mind-series">{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/12339333/arsenal-chelsea-and-tottenham-to-compete-in-mind-series-pre-season-tournament|title=Arsenal, Chelsea and Tottenham to compete in Mind Series pre-season tournament|website=[[Sky Sports]]|date=22 June 2021|access-date=14 August 2021}}</ref><ref name="si-mindseries">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/chelsea/news/official-chelsea-to-play-arsenal-and-tottenham-in-pre-season-tournament|title=Official: Chelsea to Play Arsenal And Tottenham in Pre-Season Tournament to Support Mental Health Charities|first=Nick|last=Emms|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=8 August 2021|access-date=14 August 2021}}</ref> The Gunners faced Chelsea on 1 August at [[Emirates Stadium|home]] in the first of the two matches. Manager [[Mikel Arteta]] opted to not start any of the new signings, although [[Ben White (footballer)|Ben White]] was substituted on at halftime for his debut. [[Granit Xhaka]]'s second-half header equalised after [[Kai Havertz]]'s first-half goal, but minutes later, [[Tammy Abraham]] capitalised on an Arsenal defensive error to give Chelsea the lead again. A shot from [[Joe Willock]] in the last ten minutes looked to have crossed the goal line, but without the aid of [[goal-line technology]], referee [[Andre Marriner]] did not award the goal, and the match ended 2–1 to Chelsea.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2021-Aug-01/arsenal-1-2-chelsea-match-report|title=Match report: Arsenal 1-2 Chelsea|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=1 August 2021|access-date=14 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://metro.co.uk/2021/08/01/tammy-abraham-scores-winner-as-chelsea-hold-on-to-beat-arsenal-in-pre-season-15021348/|title=Tammy Abraham scores winner as Chelsea hold on to beat Arsenal in pre-season|first=Aden-Jay|last=Wood|newspaper=[[Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]]|date=1 August 2021|access-date=14 August 2021}}</ref>

[[File:1 joe willock 2018.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Willock in 2018]]

For their last pre-season game, Arsenal played their second Mind Series match, this time [[Tottenham Hotspur Stadium|away]] to Tottenham Hotspur on 8 August, with Ben White joining fellow new signing [[Albert Sambi Lokonga]] in the starting lineup. After both teams came close to scoring on several occasions, Tottenham broke the deadlock in the 79th minute, as [[Son Heung-min]] finishing off a cross from [[Serge Aurier]] for the game's solitary goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2021-Aug-08/tottenham-hotspur-1-0-arsenal-match-report|title=Match report: Tottenham 1-0 Arsenal|first=Rob|last=Kelly|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=8 August 2021|access-date=14 August 2021}}</ref> By losing both of the matches, Arsenal finished at the bottom of the tournament, while Chelsea beat Tottenham for the inaugural title on goals scored.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/chelsea/news/official-chelsea-win-mind-series-pre-season-tournament|title=Official: Chelsea Win Mind Series Pre-Season Tournament|first=Nick|last=Emms|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=8 August 2021|access-date=14 August 2021}}</ref>

After being loaned to fellow [[Premier League]] side [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] at the end of last season's winter transfer window, Joe Willock had scored eight goals in 14 league appearances, and manager [[Steve Bruce]] was keen on bringing him back.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4202775/2021/08/13/newcastle-confirm-joe-willock-signing-from-arsenal/|title=Newcastle confirm Joe Willock signing from Arsenal|first1=Art|last1=de Roché|first2=Chris|last2=Waugh|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=13 August 2021|access-date=14 August 2021}}</ref> As a result, on 13 August, Arsenal announced the transfer of the academy graduate from the first team to Newcastle United on a six-year deal worth at least £20&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58200876|title=Joe Willock: Newcastle sign Arsenal midfielder on six-year deal|first=Alistair|last=Magowan|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=13 August 2021|access-date=14 August 2021}}</ref><ref name="willock">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/joe-willock-joins-newcastle-permanent-deal|title=Joe Willock joins Newcastle in permanent deal|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=13 August 2021|access-date=14 August 2021}}</ref>

That same day, Arsenal opened the new [[2021–22 Premier League|Premier League]] season and headed to the [[Brentford Community Stadium]] in west London to take on newly promoted [[Brentford F.C.]], who were making their Premier League debut. The Gunners began the season without Alexandre Lacazette and captain [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]], who were ruled out a few hours prior to kick-off due to illness, while Ben White and Albert Sambi Lokonga made their competitive debuts for the team.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4202773/2021/08/13/aubameyang-and-lacazette-miss-arsenals-trip-to-brentford/|title=Aubameyang and Lacazette miss Arsenal's trip to Brentford|first=David|last=Ornstein|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=13 August 2021|access-date=13 August 2021}}</ref> Academy graduate [[Folarin Balogun]] was also named to the starting lineup for his Premier League debut.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.goal.com/en-om/news/lacazette-and-aubameyang-feel-unwell-arteta-explains-absence/om5qxb6loxwj1srm4vt3gen9w|title='Lacazette and Aubameyang feel unwell' - Arteta explains absence of Arsenal's star attackers|first=Ryan|last=Tolmich|website=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|publisher=Integrated Media Company|date=13 August 2021|access-date=13 August 2021}}</ref> After [[Bryan Mbeumo]] hit the post in the 12th minute, [[Sergi Canós]] scored the opening goal of the season 10 minutes later. Meanwhile, Arsenal struggled offensively, with Kieran Tierney having their only shot on target in the first half. In the 73rd minute, [[Christian Nørgaard]] doubled Brentford's lead, heading in a long throw-in from substitute [[Mads Bech Sørensen]]. Despite several close opportunities, Arsenal were unable to find a consolation goal, and as a result, they opened the season with a 2–0 loss.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/aug/13/canos-and-nrgaard-sink-arsenal-to-give-brentford-dream-start|title=Canós and Nørgaard sink Arsenal to give Brentford dream start|first=David|last=Hynter|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=13 August 2021|access-date=13 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58109868|title=Brentford 2-0 Arsenal: Bees earn fully deserved win over Gunners|first=Phil|last=McNulty|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=13 August 2021|access-date=13 August 2021}}</ref>

[[File:Martin Ødegaard 2015-02-08 001.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Ødegaard playing for Real Madrid in 2015]]
[[File:Aaron Ramsdale February 2020.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Ramsdale playing for [[A.F.C. Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] in 2020]]

On 20 August, Arsenal announced two more signings.<ref name="odegaard-ramsdale">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/aug/20/arsenal-sign-martin-odegaard-real-madrid|title=Arsenal sign Martin Ødegaard and Aaron Ramsdale but will not stop there|first=Ben|last=Fisher|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=20 August 2021|access-date=27 August 2021}}</ref> Norwegian midfielder [[Martin Ødegaard]], who had been on loan at Arsenal from [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] for the second half of last season, joined on a permanent deal worth £34&nbsp;million.<ref name="odegaard" /> Meanwhile, English goalkeeper [[Aaron Ramsdale]] joined from [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]], which had been relegated from the Premier League [[2020–21 Premier League|last season]], in a deal worth up to £30 million.<ref name="ramsdale" />

Arsenal played the home opener of their Premier League campaign on 22 August against cross-town rivals Chelsea. The match was decided by two first-half goals, a tap-in from [[Romelu Lukaku]] and a top-corner strike from [[Reece James (footballer, born 1999)|Reece James]]. With a second consecutive 2–0 loss to open the season, Arsenal dropped to 19th, just ahead of last-placed [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] on goal difference.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/aug/22/arsenal-chelsea-premier-league-match-report|title=Ruthless Romelu Lukaku puts feeble Arsenal to the sword on Chelsea return|first=Jacob|last=Steinberg|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=22 August 2021|access-date=25 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58193457|title=Arsenal 0-2 Chelsea: Romelu Lukaku scores as Blues win London derby|first=Emlyn|last=Begley|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=22 August 2021|access-date=25 August 2021}}</ref>

On 25 August, ahead of their first [[2021–22 EFL Cup|Carabao Cup]] match of the season, Arsenal announced that [[Lucas Torreira]] would once again go out on loan, this time to [[Serie A]] team [[ACF Fiorentina]] for the entire [[2021–22 ACF Fiorentina season|2021–22 season]]. Torreira had spent the entirety of last season on loan at [[La Liga]] team [[Atlético Madrid]], accumulating 26 appearances and one goal in all competitions; Atlético Madrid went on to win the [[2020–21 La Liga|league]].<ref name="torreira">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/lucas-torreira-joins-fiorentina-loan|title=Lucas Torreira joins Fiorentina on loan|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=25 August 2021|access-date=27 August 2021}}</ref>

[[File:Lucas Torreira 2019.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Torreira in 2019]]

Arsenal entered the Carabao Cup in the [[2021–22 EFL Cup#Second round|second round]], facing [[EFL Championship|Championship]] side [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] away at [[the Hawthorns]]. Aaron Ramsdale made his debut and started in goal, while Martin Ødegaard made his first start as a full-fledged Arsenal player. With West Brom opting to field a team of mostly backup and academy players, Arsenal dominated the game from start to end. In the first half, [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]] scored two goals before [[Nicolas Pépé]] added a third in stoppage time, tapping the ball in after Aubameyang's failed bicycle kick attempt. [[Bukayo Saka]] scored five minutes into the second half before Aubameyang completed his hat-trick in the 62nd minute. Substitute Alexandre Lacazette further increased Arsenal's lead seven minutes later, and they won 6–0 to advance to the third round.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/aug/25/west-bromwich-albion-arsenal-carabao-cup-match-report|title=Aubameyang fires hat-trick in Arsenal demolition of West Brom|first=Paul|last=Doyle|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=25 August 2021|access-date=27 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58252911|title=West Brom 0-6 Arsenal: Aubameyang stars as Gunners secure first win of season|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=25 August 2021|access-date=27 August 2021}}</ref>

On 28 August, Arsenal continued their Premier League campaign, facing [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] away at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]]. A seventh-minute header from [[İlkay Gündoğan]], which Bernd Leno only managed to punch into the roof of the net, was followed by a close-range goal from [[Ferran Torres]] five minutes later. Referee [[Martin Atkinson]] showed Granit Xhaka a red card for a dangerous tackle on [[João Cancelo]] in the 35th minute. With the man advantage, Manchester City added a third goal shortly before halftime, with [[Gabriel Jesus]] redirecting a pass from [[Jack Grealish]] into the goal. Manchester City added two more goals in the second half, first with [[Rodri (footballer, born 1996)|Rodri]] early in the second half, and then with Torres scoring his second goal of the game by beating Leno to head in a cross from [[Riyad Mahrez]]. With the 5–0 result and their third consecutive loss to open their Premier League campaign, Arsenal dropped to 20th, sitting at the bottom of the table and behind both [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] and [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] on goal difference and goals scored.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/aug/28/manchester-city-arsenal-premier-league-match-report|title=Wretched 10-man Arsenal left in tatters by strikerless Manchester City|first=Richard|last=Jolly|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=28 August 2021|access-date=10 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58289653|title=Manchester City 5-0 Arsenal: Gunners suffer third league defeat in a row|first=Simon|last=Stone|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=28 August 2021|access-date=10 September 2021}}</ref>

[[File:Iran - Japan, AFC Asian Cup 2019 19.jpg|thumb|right|Tomiyasu (foreground) playing for [[Japan national football team|Japan]] against [[Iran national football team|Iran]] in the [[2019 AFC Asian Cup]] semi-finals]]

With the end of the summer transfer window approaching at the end of the month, Arsenal sought to make some final transactions. On 30 August, [[Willian (footballer, born 1988)|Willian]], who had two years remaining in his contract, left by mutual consent and returned to boyhood club [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] in Brazil.<ref name="willian">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/willian-leaves-club-mutual-consent|title=Willian leaves the club by mutual consent|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=30 August 2021|access-date=10 September 2021}}</ref> On the final day of the transfer window, three first team players were loaned out for the rest of the 2021–22 season: [[Reiss Nelson]] joined [[Feyenoord]] in the [[Eredivisie]],<ref name="reiss">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/reiss-nelson-joins-feyenoord-loan|title=Reiss Nelson joins Feyenoord on loan|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=31 August 2021|access-date=10 September 2021}}</ref> [[Rúnar Alex Rúnarsson]] joined [[Oud-Heverlee Leuven|OH Leuven]] in the [[Belgian First Division A]],<ref name="runarsson">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/alex-runarsson-joins-oh-leuven-loan|title=Alex Runarsson joins OH Leuven on loan|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=31 August 2021|access-date=10 September 2021}}</ref> and [[Héctor Bellerín]] joined [[Real Betis]] in La Liga.<ref name="bellerin">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/hector-bellerin-moves-real-betis-loan|title=Hector Bellerin moves to Real Betis on loan|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=31 August 2021|access-date=10 September 2021}}</ref> Meanwhile, the club made one deadline day signing, adding 22-year-old Japanese defender [[Takehiro Tomiyasu]] from Serie A side [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]] on a £16&nbsp;million deal.<ref name="tomiyasu" />

=== September ===
Ahead of the [[FIFA International Match Calendar|international break]], Arsenal held a [[Exhibition game#Club football|friendly]] against Brentford, to whom they had lost their first game of the Premier League campaign. The match was held behind closed doors at the [[Arsenal Training Centre]] in [[London Colney]]. After neither team scored in the first half, Arsenal scored twice early in the second half. The opener, which was scored by [[Gabriel Magalhães|Gabriel]], returning from injury, was followed by a free kick from [[Alexandre Lacazette]] at the hour mark. [[Cédric Soares|Cédric]] scored twice in the final 15 minutes to cap off the 4–0 victory and avenge Arsenal's opening day loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/match-report-arsenal-4-0-brentford|title=Match report: Arsenal 4-0 Brentford|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=2 September 2021|access-date=10 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://metro.co.uk/2021/09/02/two-key-arsenal-stars-return-in-behind-closed-doors-friendly-against-brentford-15195660/|title=Two key Arsenal stars return in behind closed doors friendly against Brentford|first=James|last=Goldman|newspaper=[[Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]]|date=2 September 2021|access-date=10 September 2021}}</ref>

After the international break, Arsenal, sitting at the bottom of the [[2021–22 Premier League|Premier League]] standings, took on 19th placed [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] at [[Emirates Stadium|home]] on 11 September. New signing [[Takehiro Tomiyasu]] made his debut, starting at right back, while Aaron Ramsdale started over Bernd Leno in goal. The match remained scoreless at halftime, though Arsenal came close on several occasions. In the 66th minute, an initial shot by [[Nicolas Pépé]] rebounded off the post back to him, and he was immediately tackled by [[Brandon Williams (footballer)|Brandon Williams]] before he could take a second shot. The ball then ricocheted off several players before Aubameyang tapped it in; a [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] check confirmed that the goal was onside, thus putting Arsenal into the lead and giving them their first Premier League goal of the season. Although Arsenal were unable to score a second goal, the 1–0 win was Arsenal's first of their Premier League campaign, and it elevated them out of the bottom three positions.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/sep/11/arsenal-norwich-premier-league-match-report|title=Aubameyang sinks Norwich to deliver Arsenal's first league win this season|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=11 September 2021|access-date=12 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58436972|title=Arsenal 1-0 Norwich City: Aubameyang scores winner as Arsenal beat Norwich|first=Phil|last=McNulty|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=11 September 2021|access-date=12 September 2021}}</ref>

Aaron Ramsdale kept his place in goal as Arsenal travelled to [[Turf Moor]] to play [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] on 18 September. After [[Ashley Westwood (footballer, born 1990)|Ashley Westwood]] clipped Bukayo Saka just outside of the penalty arc, [[Martin Ødegaard]] scored the ensuing 25-yard free kick in the 30th minute. In the 68th minute, [[Matěj Vydra]] chased down [[Ben White (footballer)|Ben White]]'s back pass to Ramsdale before being closed down and tackled in the box by the latter. Referee [[Anthony Taylor (referee)|Anthony Taylor]] awarded Burnley a penalty, having originally thought that Ramsdale made contact with Vydra before the ball, but Taylor reversed his decision after taking a second look at the incident on the pitchside VAR monitor. Neither team had many other close shots on goal, but a second consecutive 1–0 victory improved Arsenal to 13th.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/sep/18/burnley-arsenal-premier-league-match-report|title=Ødegaard's brilliance seals win for resurgent Arsenal against Burnley|first=Aaron|last=Bower|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=18 September 2021|access-date=25 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58525375|title=Burnley 0-1 Arsenal: Martin Odegaard free-kick earns Gunners second win of season|first=Simon|last=Stone|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=18 September 2021|access-date=25 September 2021}}</ref>

In the midweek match, Arsenal faced [[EFL League One]] team [[AFC Wimbledon]] on 22 September at home in the [[2021–22 EFL Cup#Third round|third round]] of the Carabao Cup.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/we-will-host-afc-wimbledon-carabao-cup|title=We will host AFC Wimbledon in Carabao Cup|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=25 August 2021|access-date=27 August 2021}}</ref> Manager [[Mikel Arteta]] fielded an almost entirely new starting eleven, with Thomas Partey the only holdover from the squad that started against Burnley and [[Eddie Nketiah]] making his season debut. Early in the match, Alexandre Lacazette converted a penalty following a foul on [[Gabriel Martinelli]]. Late in the second half, Emile Smith Rowe and Nketiah both scored in a three-minute span to secure the 3–0 victory, advancing Arsenal into the fourth round.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58566905|title=Arsenal 3-0 AFC Wimbledon: Alexandre Lacazette, Emile Smith Rowe and Eddie Nketiah score in win|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=22 September 2021|access-date=25 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2021-Sep-22/arsenal-afc-wimbledon-match-report|title=Match report: Arsenal 3-0 AFC Wimbledon|first=Rob|last=Kelly|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=22 September 2021|access-date=25 September 2021}}</ref>

[[File:Mikel Arteta (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|150px|Arteta playing for Arsenal in 2012]]

The first of two [[North London derby]] matches in the Premier League season took place on 25 September, as Arsenal hosted rivals [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] at the Emirates Stadium. In the 12th minute, Emile Smith Rowe ran in front of [[Davinson Sánchez]] to strike in a pass from Bukayo Saka past [[Hugo Lloris]]. Arsenal were on the break 15 minutes later, with Smith Rowe passing to Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang for Arsenal's second goal. A third goal came in the 34th minute, as Saka scored off the rebound after [[Harry Kane]] had tackled the ball. With just over 10 minutes to go, [[Son Heung-min]] finally scored Tottenham's first goal of the match after receiving [[Sergio Reguilón]]'s cross; Aaron Ramsdale managed to get his left hand to the ball but could not keep it out. In stoppage time, Ramsdale made a leaping save to deny a top-corner shot from [[Lucas Moura]]. The 3–1 victory was Arsenal's third in a row after losing their first three matches; meanwhile, Tottenham lost their third game in a row after starting off with three wins and topping the league table. As a result, Arsenal moved up to 10th place, tied on points and goal difference with Tottenham in 11th but ahead due to goals scored.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/sep/26/rampant-arsenal-claim-derby-spoils-as-first-half-goal-blitz-sinks-tottenham|title=Rampant Arsenal claim derby spoils as first-half goal blitz sinks Tottenham|first=David|last=Hytner|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=25 September 2021|access-date=28 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58613174|title=Arsenal 3-1 Tottenham: Gunners defeat north London rivals at Emirates Stadium|first=Phil|last=McNulty|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=25 September 2021|access-date=28 September 2021}}</ref>

After guiding Arsenal to wins in all three of their Premier League matches of the month, manager Mikel Arteta was named as the [[Premier League Manager of the Month]] over [[Pep Guardiola]] ([[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]), [[Jürgen Klopp]] ([[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]), [[Graham Potter]] ([[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]]), and [[Dean Smith (footballer, born 1971)|Dean Smith]] ([[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]]). This was Arteta's first Manager of the Month award and the first for an Arsenal manager since [[Arsène Wenger]]'s October 2015 award.<ref name="arteta-sep-ars">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arteta-named-pl-manager-month|title=🏆 Arteta named PL Manager of the Month|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=8 October 2021|access-date=25 October 2021}}</ref><ref name="arteta-sep-pl">{{cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/2282126|title=Arteta named September 2021 Barclays Manager of the Month|publisher=[[Premier League]]|date=8 October 2021|access-date=25 October 2021}}</ref>

=== October ===
Arsenal's first match of the month was a Premier League match away to [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] at the [[Falmer Stadium|Amex Stadium]] on 2 October. [[Albert Sambi Lokonga]] played in place of [[Granit Xhaka]], who had been ruled out for up to three months after suffering a knee injury in the match against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/12421115/granit-xhaka-arsenal-midfielder-ruled-out-up-to-three-months-with-knee-injury|title=Granit Xhaka: Arsenal midfielder ruled out up to three months with knee injury|website=[[Sky Sports]]|date=29 September 2021|access-date=2 October 2021}}</ref> In the last few minutes of the match, penalty claims from Brighton for a shove on [[Shane Duffy]] by [[Gabriel Magalhães|Gabriel]] were dismissed by VAR. Neither team was able to score all game, though Brighton had the majority of possession as well as 21 shots to Arsenal's eight; of these shots, both teams had two on target.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/oct/02/brighton-arsenal-premier-league-match-report|title=Arsenal hold off Brighton in stalemate as Mikel Arteta accepts 'point gained'|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=2 October 2021|access-date=2 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58667889|title=Brighton & Hove Albion 0-0 Arsenal: Wasteful Seagulls held by Gunners|first=Matthew|last=Howarth|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=2 October 2021|access-date=2 October 2021}}</ref>

During the international break, Arsenal hosted fellow London side [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.]] from the [[EFL Championship]] for a closed-door friendly match at the [[Arsenal Training Centre|London Colney]] training ground on 6 October. Arsenal won 3–2, although the goal scorers for either team were not made publicly known.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://dailycannon.com/2021/10/arsenal-qpr-friendly-behind-closed-doors/|title=Arsenal beat QPR 3-2 in behind-closed-doors friendly|first=Dan|last=Critchlow|website=Daily Cannon|date=7 October 2021|access-date=27 November 2021}}</ref>

On 18 October, Arsenal took on south London side [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], managed by former Arsenal player [[Patrick Vieira]]. In the eighth minute, a shot from [[Nicolas Pépé]] was parried by goalkeeper [[Vicente Guaita]] to [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]], who beat [[James McArthur]] to tap in the rebound. Crystal Palace equalized early in the second half; after [[Jordan Ayew]] dispossessed [[Thomas Partey]], [[Christian Benteke]] scored with the rebound. In the 73rd minute, after [[Conor Gallagher]] dispossessed Albert Sambi Lokonga and Crystal Palace were on the break, [[Odsonne Édouard]] scored off the underside of the crossbar to give Crystal Palace the lead. Arsenal finally drew even in the fifth minute of stoppage time, with a shot from Ben White deflected by Guaita into the path of substitute [[Alexandre Lacazette]] for a tap-in, and the game ended 2–2.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/oct/18/arsenal-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report|title=Lacazette saves Arsenal with last-gasp equaliser to deny Vieira's Crystal Palace|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=18 October 2021|access-date=25 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58866457|title=Arsenal 2-2 Crystal Palace: Alexandre Lacazette rescues Gunners with late goal|first=Emlyn|last=Begley|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=18 October 2021|access-date=25 October 2021}}</ref>

In their second Premier League match at [[Emirates Stadium|home]] in four days, 12th-placed Arsenal hosted 13th-placed [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]]. Left-back Kieran Tierney missed his first Premier League match of the season due to a bruised right ankle, thus giving [[Nuno Tavares]] his first Premier League start.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://metro.co.uk/2021/10/22/arsenal-explain-kieran-tierneys-absence-from-squad-to-face-aston-villa-15472164/|title=Arsenal explain Kieran Tierney's absence from squad to face Aston Villa as Alexandre Lacazette starts|first=Aden-Jay|last=Wood|newspaper=[[Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]]|date=22 October 2021|access-date=25 October 2021}}</ref> Thomas Partey scored a header off [[Emile Smith Rowe]]'s corner in the 23rd minute for his first Arsenal goal. In first-half stoppage time, referee [[Craig Pawson]] consulted the pitchside VAR monitor for [[Matt Targett]]'s challenge on Alexandre Lacazette and awarded Arsenal a penalty. Former Arsenal goalkeeper [[Emiliano Martínez]] saved Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang's initial shot by diving down to his left, but Aubameyang tapped in the rebound. Ten minutes into the second half, Smith Rowe intercepted a pass from [[John McGinn]] to [[Matty Cash]], with the ball rebounding to Albert Sambi Lokonga, who passed out wide to Tavares. Tavares's through pass to Aubameyang was then flicked forward to Smith Rowe, who continued his run before eventually firing a shot that deflected off [[Tyrone Mings]] and the near post past Martínez. Aston Villa were able to score a consolation goal late in the match when [[Leon Bailey]]'s run along the edge of the box took the ball into the path of [[Jacob Ramsey]], whose first-time shot found the top corner, but Arsenal hung on for the 3–1 victory.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/oct/22/arsenal-aston-villa-premier-league-match-report|title=Emile Smith Rowe excels as Arsenal sweep aside uninspired Aston Villa|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=22 October 2021|access-date=25 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58921467|title=Arsenal 3-1 Aston Villa: Gunners hit three past lacklustre Villa|first=Emlyn|last=Begley|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=22 October 2021|access-date=25 October 2021}}</ref>

In the midweek match at home against fellow Premier League club [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] on 26 October in the [[2021–22 EFL Cup#Fourth round|fourth round]] of the EFL Cup, Bernd Leno made his first start in goal since the previous round's match against [[AFC Wimbledon]] a month ago. Neither team scored in the first half, but ten minutes into the second half, [[Calum Chambers]] was substituted on in place of an injured Ben White before scoring the opening goal 23 seconds later. After Emile Smith Rowe's corner was headed around the box by [[Eddie Nketiah]] and Nicolas Pépé, Chambers beat [[Jack Harrison (footballer, born 1996)|Jack Harrison]] to the header; referee [[Andre Marriner]] confirmed that the ball had crossed the goal line before [[Illan Meslier]] could parry the ball away. On 69 minutes, Arsenal doubled their lead when Nketiah intercepted a backwards header from Leeds captain [[Liam Cooper]] to Meslier, guided the ball over Meslier, and slotted in the goal from a narrow angle; this was Nketiah's second goal in as many appearances all season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/oct/26/arsenal-leeds-united-carabao-cup-match-report|title=Calum Chambers' instant impact sends Arsenal on way to Leeds win|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=26 October 2021|access-date=26 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58963260|title=Arsenal 2-0 Leeds United: Goalscorer Eddie Nketiah has future at club, says Mikel Arteta|first=Alex|last=Bysouth|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=26 October 2021|access-date=26 October 2021}}</ref> The 2–0 result advanced Arsenal to the quarter-finals, in which they were drawn at home against [[EFL League One|League One]] team [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/well-face-sunderland-carabao-cup|title=We'll face Sunderland in the Carabao Cup|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=30 October 2021|access-date=30 October 2021}}</ref>

Arsenal finished the month away to [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] at the [[King Power Stadium]] on 30 October, with the match being decided by two early goals. After [[Daniel Amartey]] nearly scored an own goal in the opening minute, Gabriel scored a header, and his first goal of the season, in the fifth minute on a corner from Bukayo Saka, who was making his 100th senior club appearance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/leicester-vs-arsenal-live-score-and-result-updates-premier-league-latest-with-aaron-ramsdale-in-superb-form/TejfMRnFyGEK/|title=Leicester vs Arsenal live score and result updates: Premier League latest as Gabriel and Smith Rowe score|first=Ed|last=Mackey|publisher=[[The Athletic]]|date=30 October 2021|access-date=20 October 2021}}</ref> In the eighteenth minute, Alexandre Lacazette received a pass from Saka before running into a crowd of Leicester defenders in the box. After [[Jonny Evans]] dispossessed Lacazette, [[Luke Thomas (footballer, born 2001)|Luke Thomas]]'s attempted clearance fell to Emile Smith Rowe, who fired in the second goal. Meanwhile, Aaron Ramsdale made several key saves in a performance that earned him his first Man of the Match as an Arsenal player. Among these was a leaping save near the end of the first half to parry a [[James Maddison]] free kick onto the crossbar before Evans's shot from the rebound was cleared off the line by Thomas Partey. The 2–0 victory extended Arsenal's unbeaten streak since the beginning of September to seven matches in the league and nine in all competitions.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/oct/30/leicester-arsenal-premier-league-match-report|title=Aaron Ramsdale excels as Arsenal beat Leicester to extend unbeaten streak|first=Jonathan|last=Liew|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=30 October 2021|access-date=30 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59019332|title=Leicester City 0-2 Arsenal: Mikel Arteta's side extend unbeaten run with fine victory over Foxes|first=Steve|last=Sutcliffe|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=30 October 2021|access-date=30 October 2021}}</ref>

Arsenal's successful defensive performances led to Aaron Ramsdale being nominated for the Premier League's [[Premier League Player of the Month|Player of the Month Award]], which was ultimately won by [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]'s [[Mohamed Salah]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/2325837|title=Shortlist for October 2021 EA SPORTS Player of the Month|publisher=[[Premier League]]|date=6 November 2021|access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/2347037|title=Salah wins October 2021 EA SPORTS Player of the Month award|publisher=[[Premier League]]|date=12 November 2021|access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref>

=== November ===
On 7 November, Arsenal faced [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] at [[Emirates Stadium|home]]. In the seventh minute, [[Ainsley Maitland-Niles]] dispossessed [[Ismaïla Sarr]] before [[Alexandre Lacazette]]'s chipped ball was deflected by [[Ben Foster (footballer)|Ben Foster]] to [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]]. Aubameyang's first touch then took the ball into the path of [[Bukayo Saka]], whose shot went in between [[Nicolas Nkoulou]] and a recovering Foster for what seemed to be the opening goal. However, while Saka was in front of Nkoulou, he was also behind of Foster, thus making him offside, and the goal was disallowed. In the 34th minute, referee [[Kevin Friend]] awarded Arsenal a penalty after [[Danny Rose (footballer, born 1990)|Danny Rose]] ran into Lacazette, who was trying to control an errant shot from Maitland-Niles. Foster then saved Aubameyang's penalty before recovering the rebound. In the 56th minute, [[Ben White (footballer)|Ben White]] regained possession of the ball in the Arsenal offensive third and ran forward, evading [[Juraj Kucka]] and [[Joshua King (footballer, born 1992)|Joshua King]] before running into [[Moussa Sissoko]]. The ball then fell to [[Emile Smith Rowe]] on the edge of the box, who fired into the far corner for what would be the match's only goal, as well as Smith Rowe's third goal in as many Premier League matches. [[Martin Ødegaard]] nearly scored a second goal on 73 minutes, but Aubameyang, who had been in an offside position, touched the ball right before it crossed the goal line. In the 89th minute, Kucka, who was already on a yellow card after a foul on Lacazette in the first half, was shown a second yellow card for a foul on [[Nuno Tavares]] and was sent off. The 1–0 victory continued Arsenal's rise up the table, as they moved into fifth place.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/nov/07/arsenal-watford-premier-league-match-report|title=Emile Smith Rowe leads Arsenal's resurgence with victory over Watford|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=7 November 2021|access-date=7 November 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59107413|title=Arsenal 1-0 Watford: Claudio Ranieri accuses Mikel Arteta's side of a lack of respect|first=Harry|last=Poole|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=7 November 2021|access-date=7 November 2021}}</ref>

After the international break, Arsenal travelled to [[Anfield]] to take on [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] on 20 November. After there was contact between [[Takehiro Tomiyasu]] and [[Sadio Mané]] as the players were challenging for a header, managers [[Mikel Arteta]] and [[Jürgen Klopp]] engaged in a verbal dispute on the sideline, for which referee [[Michael Oliver (referee)|Michael Oliver]] showed a yellow card to both managers. After Mané and [[Mohamed Salah]] were both denied by point-blank saves from Aaron Ramsdale earlier in the game, Mané headed a [[Trent Alexander-Arnold]] free kick into the ground and away from Ramsdale for the opening goal in the 39th minute. Early in the second half, [[Diogo Jota]] added a second goal for Liverpool after intercepting a backwards pass from [[Nuno Tavares]]. In the 73rd minute, a fast break by Liverpool was finished off with Mané centering the ball for Salah to finish from close range. Four minutes later, [[Takumi Minamino]], having just been substituted into the match, slotted home Alexander-Arnold's cross at the back post after just 48 seconds on the pitch. The 4–0 defeat ended Arsenal's unbeaten run at eight matches in the league and 10 in all competitions, although they remained in fifth.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/nov/20/liverpool-arsenal-premier-league-match-report|title=Sadio Mané leads Liverpool's 4-0 thrashing to end Arsenal's unbeaten run|first=Andy|last=Hunter|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=20 November 2021|access-date=20 November 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59271459|title=Liverpool 4-0 Arsenal: Reds end Arsenal's 10-game unbeaten run|first=Emma|last=Sanders|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=20 November 2021|access-date=20 November 2021}}</ref>

Arsenal rebounded seven days later against bottom-of-the-table [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] and new manager [[Eddie Howe]], who made his debut in the Newcastle dugout; Howe had missed his first match the previous week in quarantine after testing positive for COVID-19.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11678/12479135/eddie-howe-newcastle-head-coach-will-be-in-dugout-for-match-against-arsenal-after-testing-negative-for-covid-19|title=Eddie Howe: Newcastle head coach will be in dugout for match against Arsenal after testing negative for Covid-19|website=[[Sky Sports]]|date=27 November 2021|access-date=27 November 2021}}</ref> Neither team was able to score in the first half. [[Jonjo Shelvey]] came closest for Newcastle in the 30th minute, with his shot parried onto the crossbar by Aaron Ramsdale. Shortly before halftime, after Emile Smith Rowe's header was saved by [[Martin Dúbravka]], Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang missed from close range and kicked the rebound against the outside of the post. In the 56th minute, Bukayo Saka passed back to Smith Rowe, who passed infield to [[Nuno Tavares]]; meanwhile, Saka had continued his run forward, and after receiving the ball from Tavares, he fired a low shot into the far corner past Dúbravka for the opening goal. Eight minutes later, Saka was forced off with an injury and was replaced by [[Gabriel Martinelli]]. Less than two minutes after coming on, Martinelli finished off a chipped pass from Takehiro Tomiyasu with a first-time volley to bolster Arsenal's lead. Arsenal maintained their 2–0 lead to win the match and stay in fifth place.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/nov/27/arsenal-newcastle-premier-league-match-report|title=Arsenal's Bukayo Saka and Gabriel Martinelli see off winless Newcastle|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=27 November 2021|access-date=27 November 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59356976|title=Arsenal 2-0 Newcastle United: Bukayo Saka and Gabriel Martinelli sink Eddie Howe's side|first=Emlyn|last=Begley|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=27 November 2021|access-date=27 November 2021}}</ref>

=== December ===
Arsenal began December with a midweek fixture at [[Old Trafford]] on 2 December away to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], who were led by caretaker manager [[Michael Carrick]] in his last game before interim manager [[Ralf Rangnick]] taking over.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/manchester-united-engman_utd/story/4537668/man-united-interim-manager-michael-carrick-leaves-club-with-immediate-effect-as-rangnick-era-looms|title=Man United interim manager Michael Carrick leaves club with immediate effect as Rangnick era looms|first=Rob|last=Dawson|website=[[ESPN]]|date=2 December 2021|access-date=3 December 2021}}</ref> From a 13th minute corner by [[Martin Ødegaard]], [[Emile Smith Rowe]] scored the opening goal from outside of the box, with the assist from [[Mohamed Elneny]] after [[Harry Maguire]]'s initial clearance. Referee [[Martin Atkinson]] was initially hesitant to award the goal, as goalkeeper [[David de Gea]] lay injured after having his ankle stepped on by his teammate [[Fred (footballer, born 1993)|Fred]], but the goal was made official after VAR review. Shortly before halftime, Manchester United equalized after [[Jadon Sancho]] passed infield to Fred, who squared the ball for [[Bruno Fernandes]] to slot it in past Aaron Ramsdale. In the 52nd minute, the home side took the lead as [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] finished off [[Marcus Rashford]]'s low cross. However, Arsenal equalized less than two minutes later; on the right flank, [[Gabriel Martinelli]] received [[Thomas Partey]]'s through pass before firing a low cross into the box for Ødegaard, whose shot curled in past the reach of de Gea. In the 68th minute, Atkinson initially did not award a penalty to Manchester United after Ødegaard's tackle on Fred, but he reversed his decision after consulting the pitchside VAR monitor. Ronaldo scored again, converting the penalty for his 800th career goal and the decisive goal of the match. Despite the 3–2 defeat, Arsenal remained in fifth place for the fourth consecutive matchweek.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/02/manchester-united-arsenal-premier-league-match-report|title=Cristiano Ronaldo seals Manchester United's fightback victory over Arsenal|first=David|last=Hytner|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=2 December 2021|access-date=3 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59411776|title=Man Utd 3-2 Arsenal: Cristiano Ronaldo passes 800 goals in win tinged with controversy|first=Simon|last=Stone|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=2 December 2021|access-date=3 December 2021}}</ref>

Four days later, Arsenal lost their second game in a row after playing away to [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] at [[Goodison Park]], with [[Granit Xhaka]] making his return from injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://metro.co.uk/2021/12/06/im-back-granit-xhaka-announces-return-to-arsenal-squad-for-everton-clash-15725526/|title='I'm back!' – Granit Xhaka announces return to Arsenal squad for Everton clash|first=Mike|last=Stavrou|newspaper=[[Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]]|date=6 December 2021|access-date=15 December 2021}}</ref> Minutes before halftime, a free kick from [[Andros Townsend]] was headed in by [[Richarlison]], but the goal was disallowed as the latter was found to be offside by VAR. However, in first-half stoppage time, Arsenal scored the opening goal with Martin Ødegaard slotting in a cross from [[Kieran Tierney]] with a side-foot volley. In the 56th minute, Richarlison seemed to have scored after receiving a pass from [[Abdoulaye Doucouré]], but he was ruled offside by VAR again. Richarlison was finally able to score in the 80th minute, as he headed in the rebound after a [[Demarai Gray]] shot from outside the box hit the crossbar. After [[Eddie Nketiah]] missed a close-range header in the 84th minute, Gray scored Everton's second goal of the game in the second of six minutes of stoppage time. Gray's winning strike, which came from a similar location to the one that hit the crossbar, hit off the far post and into the goal, resulting in a 2–1 loss for Arsenal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/06/everton-arsenal-premier-league-match-report|title=Demarai Gray stunner and Richarlison earn Everton vital victory over Arsenal|first=Andy|last=Hunter|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=6 December 2021|access-date=11 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59455893|title=Everton 2-1 Arsenal: Demarai Gray stoppage-time goal earns victory for Rafael Benitez's men|first=Alistair|last=Magowan|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=6 December 2021|access-date=11 December 2021}}</ref>

[[File:1 Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|200px|Aubameyang in 2018]]

On 11 December, Arsenal returned home to the [[Emirates Stadium]] for a match against a depleted [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] side, who were without several key outfield players and both first-choice goalkeepers, with emergency goalkeeper [[Willy Caballero]] starting after signing earlier in the week.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/arsenal-southampton-forwards-aubameyang-b971152.html|title=Floundering Arsenal forwards must seize chance against ravaged Southampton as resurgence hits the skids|first=Simon|last=Collings|newspaper=[[Evening Standard]]|date=10 December 2021|access-date=11 December 2021}}</ref> Meanwhile, Arsenal themselves started without captain [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]], who had reportedly been dropped to the bench for a 'disciplinary breach' by manager [[Mikel Arteta]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/11/arsenal-drop-club-captain-aubameyang-from-squad-for-disciplinary-breach|title=
Arsenal drop club captain Aubameyang from squad for 'disciplinary breach'|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=11 December 2021|access-date=11 December 2021}}</ref> In the 21st minute, Arsenal scored first after playing out from the back, as a series of passes down the length of the pitch culminated with [[Bukayo Saka]]'s low cutback being finished off by [[Alexandre Lacazette]]. Six minutes later, Arsenal doubled their lead. After Kieran Tierney received [[Takehiro Tomiyasu]]'s high pass at the back post, his cross was blocked by [[Tino Livramento]]; however, Tierney recovered the rebound and headed the ball to Martin Ødegaard, who scored a header for his third goal in as many matches. After [[Gabriel Magalhães|Gabriel]] had a tap-in disallowed for being offside in the 59th minute, he headed in a corner from Gabriel Martinelli three minutes later. Arsenal continued to apply pressure to Southampton in the search of a fourth goal, but both Martinelli and Saka hit the posts with their shots. Meanwhile, Aaron Ramsdale made six saves to secure the clean sheet and a 3–0 win.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/11/arsenal-southampton-premier-league-match-report|title=Arsenal stroll past Southampton after Arteta drops Aubameyang|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=11 December 2021|access-date=11 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59455893|title=Arsenal 3-0 Southampton: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang dropped ahead of win|first=Joe|last=Rindl|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=11 December 2021|access-date=11 December 2021}}</ref>

The day before the home match against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] on 15 December, the club announced that Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang would be stripped of the club captaincy due to repeated disciplinary breaches and would not be considered for the West Ham match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/club-update-pierre-emerick-aubameyang|title=Club update: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=14 December 2021|access-date=15 December 2021}}</ref> Manager Mikel Arteta elaborated that the captaincy would be shared among a "'leadership group' of senior players," including Alexandre Lacazette and Granit Xhaka, the latter of whom had preceded Aubameyang as captain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3686962/2021/12/14/arsenal-to-rely-on-leadership-group-after-stripping-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-of-captaincy/|title=Arsenal to rely on 'leadership group' after stripping Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang of captaincy|first1=James|last1=McNicholas|first2=Art|last2=de Roché|publisher=[[The Athletic]]|date=14 December 2021|access-date=15 December 2021}}</ref>

After Alexandre Lacazette had assumed the captaincy role against Southampton, manager Mikel Arteta opted to retain him as captain against West Ham.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football.london/arsenal-fc/news/mikel-arteta-arsenal-alexandre-lacazette-22476468|title=Mikel Arteta reveals reason for Alexandre Lacazette being Arsenal captain for West Ham clash|first1=Bobby|last1=Vincent|first2=Jake|last2=Stokes|website=[[football.london]]|publisher=[[Reach plc]]|date=15 December 2021|access-date=15 December 2021}}</ref> Three minutes into the second half, Lacazette played a through pass to Gabriel Martinelli, who ran past the West Ham defense and curled in the opening goal. In the 67th minute, [[Vladimír Coufal]], who was already on a yellow card after contact with Kieran Tierney in the 11th minute, was sent off after a second yellow card following a tackle on Lacazette in the box. For the same foul, referee [[Anthony Taylor (referee)|Anthony Taylor]] awarded Arsenal a penalty, which Lacazette took but was saved by [[Łukasz Fabiański]]. On 87 minutes, after Takehiro Tomiyasu dispossessed [[Saïd Benrahma]], Bukayo Saka recovered the ball before passing it near the center line to substitute Emile Smith Rowe, who continued his run and scored a second goal for Arsenal. The 2–0 victory moved Arsenal into the top four for the first time all season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/15/arsenal-west-ham-premier-league-match-report|title=Arsenal go fourth as Martinelli and Smith Rowe sink 10-man West Ham|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=15 December 2021|access-date=15 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59573768|title=Arsenal 2-0 West Ham: Gunners move up to fourth with victory over 10-man Hammers|first=Emma|last=Sanders|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=15 December 2021|access-date=15 December 2021}}</ref>

With a rise in positive [[COVID-19 pandemic in England|COVID-19]] test results forcing the postponement of the other five matches scheduled for 18 December, Arsenal's match away to an injury-stricken [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] at [[Elland Road]] was the only remaining [[Premier League]] fixture that day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/aston-villa-vs-burnley-off-as-latest-premier-league-fixture/blt2797ba180e36d95c|title=Aston Villa vs Burnley off as latest Premier League fixture postponed amid Covid-19 surge|first=Andrew|last=Steel|website=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=18 December 2021|access-date=18 December 2021}}</ref> In the 16th minute, after Alexandre Lacazette dispossessed [[Adam Forshaw]] in the box, Gabriel Martinelli recovered the loose ball and fired it in first time for the opening goal; this goal was Arsenal's 7,000th scored in the top flight of English football.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2021-Dec-18/leeds-1-4-arsenal-match-report|title=Match report: Leeds 1-4 Arsenal|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=18 December 2021|access-date=23 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/analysis-our-7000-top-flight-goals|title=Analysis: Our 7,000 top-flight goals|first=Josh|last=James|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=20 December 2021|access-date=23 December 2021}}</ref> Twelve minutes later, Granit Xhaka intercepted a pass from [[Stuart Dallas]] intended for [[Mateusz Klich]] near midfield and played a through pass to Martinelli, who scored to double Arsenal's lead. Three minutes from halftime, Bukayo Saka scored the third goal after his shot deflected off Klich's foot and past [[Illan Meslier]]. Notably, Arsenal's 11 shots on target in the first half were the most in the first half of all Premier League matches since the [[2003–04 FA Premier League|2003–04]] season (also the season of the [[2003–04 Arsenal F.C. season|Invincibles]]), when [[Opta Sports|Opta]] began recording such statistics. After [[Ben White (footballer)|Ben White]]'s tackle on [[Joe Gelhardt]], referee [[Andre Marriner]] awarded Leeds a penalty, which [[Raphinha (footballer, born 1996)|Raphinha]] converted in the 75th minute. Substitute Emile Smith Rowe capped off the match by finishing off a pass from Martin Ødegaard to give Arsenal a 4–1 win.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/18/leeds-arsenal-premier-league-match-report|title=Gabriel Martinelli double helps sink Leeds to continue Arsenal's upturn|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=18 December 2021|access-date=18 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59618480|title=Leeds 1-4 Arsenal: Gabriel Martinelli scores twice in Gunners win|first=Thomas|last=Mallows|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=18 December 2021|access-date=18 December 2021}}</ref>

On 21 December, Arsenal hosted [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] in the [[2021–22 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] quarter-finals, with [[Nicolas Pépé]] making his 100th appearance for Arsenal. [[Cédric Soares|Cédric]]'s corner in the 17th minute was headed towards goal by [[Rob Holding]], only for [[Lee Burge]] to parry the ball into the path of [[Eddie Nketiah]], who continued his three-match run of scoring in the EFL Cup and put in the tap-in from close range. In the 27th minute, Pépé received a cutback from Cédric and fired a shot, which was deflected by [[Callum Doyle]] into the roof of the net to double Arsenal's lead. However, Sunderland scored four minutes later, as [[Nathan Broadhead]] received a through pass from [[Elliot Embleton]] and lifted the ball over an onrushing Bernd Leno into the goal. Four minutes into the second half, Nketiah scored his second goal, stepping in front of Doyle to redirect a low cross from [[Nuno Tavares]]. In the 58th minute, Nketiah completed his hat trick, beating [[Tom Flanagan (footballer)|Tom Flanagan]] to a pass from Pépé and scoring with a backheel finish. In second half stoppage time, Pépé once again provided the assist, this time to [[Charlie Patino]], who had been substituted on ten minutes prior for his senior team debut and slid the ball in past Burge. The 5–1 result advanced Arsenal to the semi-finals for the first time since the [[2017–18 EFL Cup|2017–18 edition]], while Nketiah's hat trick made him the joint top goalscorer with [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]]'s [[Marcus Forss]] on five goals.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-sunderland/report/460049|title=Arsenal 5-1 Sunderland: Eddie Nketiah scores hat-trick to steer Gunners into Carabao Cup semi-finals|website=[[Sky Sports]]|date=21 December 2021|access-date=22 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59646904|title=Carabao Cup, Arsenal 5-1 Sunderland: Eddie Nketiah scores superb hat-trick|first=Alex|last=Bysouth|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=21 December 2021|access-date=22 December 2021}}</ref>

Arsenal then headed to [[Carrow Road]] for a [[Boxing Day#Sport|Boxing Day]] match against [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]]. Bukayo Saka scored the opening goal in the sixth minute after receiving a pass from Martin Ødegaard and shooting through the legs of [[Brandon Williams (footballer)|Brandon Williams]]. Arsenal's second goal was also assisted by Ødegaard, as he found Kieran Tierney on the left flank, who ran into the box and fired a low shot across goal just before halftime. In the 67th minute, Saka scored again after receiving a pass from Alexandre Lacazette and beating Williams one-on-one before shooting from the edge of the box. [[Ozan Kabak]] tripped Lacazette as the latter was receiving a pass from Emile Smith Rowe, prompting referee [[Graham Scott (referee)|Graham Scott]] to award Arsenal a penalty in the 84th minute, which Lacazette then converted. In second half stoppage time, substitute Nicolas Pépé's pass across the box deflected off Kabak to Smith Rowe, who finished at the back post for his third goal in as many matches, all of which have come as a substitute. The 5–0 win meant that Arsenal ended the year on a four-match win streak.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/26/norwich-arsenal-premier-league-match-report|title=Bukayo Saka's double leads Arsenal's 5-0 Boxing Day breeze past Norwich|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=26 December 2021|access-date=26 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59403659|title=Norwich City 0-5 Arsenal: Bukayo Saka scores twice as Gunners heap misery on Canaries|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=26 December 2021|access-date=26 December 2021}}</ref>

Arsenal's performances in December led to several Premier League monthly award nominations. Alexandre Lacazette's goal to finish off a 'flowing' team move against Southampton was nominated for [[Premier League Goal of the Month|Goal of the Month]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/lacazette-premier-league-goal-of-the-month-vote|title=Lacazette nominated for PL Goal of the Month|first=Samuel|last=Gilbert|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=3 January 2022|access-date=7 January 2022}}</ref><ref name="laca-dec-ars">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/lacazette-wins-pl-goal-month-award|title=Lacazette wins PL Goal of the Month award|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=14 January 2022|access-date=14 January 2022}}</ref> while manager Mikel Arteta was nominated for [[Premier League Manager of the Month|Manager of the Month]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/arteta-premier-league-manager-of-the-month-vote|title=Arteta nominated for PL Manager of the Month|first=Samuel|last=Gilbert|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=3 January 2022|access-date=7 January 2022}}</ref> Additionally, both Martin Ødegaard and Gabriel Martinelli were nominated for [[Premier League Player of the Month|Player of the Month]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/premier-league-player-of-the-month-odegaard-martinelli-vote|title=Odegaard, Martinelli up for PL Player of the Month|first=Samuel|last=Gilbert|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=3 January 2022|access-date=7 January 2022}}</ref> Though the latter two awards were ultimately won by [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]'s [[Pep Guardiola]] and [[Raheem Sterling]], respectively,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/2444570|title=Guardiola claims Barclays Manager of the Month award|publisher=[[Premier League]]|date=14 January 2022|access-date=14 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/2444493|title=Sterling wins EA SPORTS Player of the Month award|publisher=[[Premier League]]|date=14 January 2022|access-date=14 January 2022}}</ref> Lacazette's goal was named the Goal of the Month.<ref name="laca-dec-ars" /><ref name="laca-dec-pl">{{cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/2444769|title=Lacazette strike voted Budweiser Goal of the Month|publisher=[[Premier League]]|date=14 January 2022|access-date=14 January 2022}}</ref>

=== January ===
[[File:1 Ainsley Maitland-Niles 2018 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|150px|Maitland-Niles in 2018]]

In the first [[Premier League]] fixture of 2022, Arsenal hosted [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] at the [[Emirates Stadium]] on New Year's Day. Dutch assistant manager [[Albert Stuivenberg]] filled in for manager [[Mikel Arteta]], who had tested positive for COVID-19 on 29 December and was forced to miss the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/albert-stuivenberg-press-conference-transcript-arsenal-man-city-premier-league|title=Stuivenberg on the result, decisions and Mikel|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=1 January 2022|access-date=1 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/31/mikel-arteta-frustrated-watch-arsenal-from-afar-covid-albert-stuivenberg|title='I will need a big room': Arteta frustrated at having to watch Arsenal from afar|first=Ed|last=Aarons|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=31 December 2021|access-date=1 January 2022}}</ref> An Arsenal penalty call in the 10th minute after contact between [[Martin Ødegaard]] and [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]] was dismissed by VAR. However, Arsenal took the lead after the half-hour mark when [[Kieran Tierney]] found [[Bukayo Saka]] in the box, who slotted the ball in as [[Alexandre Lacazette]] screened off [[Nathan Aké]]. Manchester City equalized when [[Riyad Mahrez]] converted a 57th-minute penalty, which had been awarded by referee [[Stuart Attwell]] after he deemed [[Granit Xhaka]] to have committed a foul on [[Bernardo Silva]]. Immediately following the restart, Aké made a goal line clearance on [[Aymeric Laporte]]'s header to prevent the own goal before [[Gabriel Martinelli]] missed the follow-up just wide of the top corner. Less than a minute later, Attwell sent off [[Gabriel Magalhães|Gabriel]] after the latter picked up a second yellow card for a foul on [[Gabriel Jesus]]; Attwell had shown him his first yellow card following the Mahrez penalty for dissent. With Manchester City having the man advantage, [[Rodri (footballer, born 1996)|Rodri]] scored the winning goal in stoppage time after Laporte's initial shot had been blocked by [[Ben White (footballer)|Ben White]], giving the visitors a 2–1 win.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/jan/01/arsenal-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report|title=Rodri's injury-time strike gives City win as 10-man Arsenal blame VAR|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=1 January 2022|access-date=1 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59787808|title=Arsenal 1-2 Manchester City: Rodri scores late winner|first=Alex|last=Bysouth|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=1 January 2022|access-date=1 January 2022}}</ref>

On 5 January, it was announced that the first leg of the [[2021–22 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] semi-finals against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], which was to be held the following day, was postponed to 13 January due to a [[COVID-19]] outbreak among Liverpool's players and staff, with the second leg to be played a week later. This also led a change in the home team order, with Liverpool now hosting the first leg and Arsenal hosting the second leg.<ref name="efl-sf-1">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/jan/05/liverpool-covid-arsenal-carabao-cup|title=Liverpool's Carabao Cup semi-final at Arsenal postponed after EFL ruling|first=Andy|last=Hunter|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=5 January 2022|access-date=5 January 2022}}</ref>

Ahead of the [[2021 Africa Cup of Nations|Africa Cup of Nations]], five players were called up by their respective countries; these were [[Mohamed Elneny]] ([[Egypt national football team|Egypt]]), [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]] ([[Gabon national football team|Gabon]]), [[Thomas Partey]] ([[Ghana national football team|Ghana]]), and [[Nicolas Pépé]] ([[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]]), with academy player [[Omar Rekik]] also being called up for [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/africa-cup-of-nations-preview-aubameyang-partey-pepe-premier-league|title=Africa Cup of Nations: Who's playing and when?|first=Samuel|last=Gilbert|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=3 January 2022|access-date=7 January 2022}}</ref>

Ahead of the [[2021–22 FA Cup|FA Cup]] third-round match against [[EFL Championship]] club [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] on 9 January, the club announced the release of a one-off, all-white fourth kit that would be worn during the match. The kit, which is not commercially available and will be "awarded to individuals who are making a positive difference in the community," is part of a campaign to raise awareness about knife crime and youth violence, which contributed to the highest number of teenage murders in a year in London since records began.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/12508059/arsenal-to-remove-red-from-shirt-and-play-in-all-white-in-fa-cup-as-part-of-adidas-anti-knife-crime-collaboration|title=Arsenal to remove red from shirt and play in all-white in FA Cup as part of adidas anti-knife crime collaboration|first=Dev|last=Trehan|work=[[Sky Sports]]|date=7 January 2022|access-date=8 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-and-adidas-no-more-red|title=Arsenal and adidas: No More Red|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=5 January 2022|access-date=8 January 2022}}</ref>

On 8 January, [[Ainsley Maitland-Niles]] joined [[Serie A]] club [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref name="amn">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/ainsley-maitland-niles-joins-roma-loan-transfer-window|title=Ainsley Maitland-Niles joins AS Roma on loan|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=8 January 2022|access-date=8 January 2022}}</ref>

Arsenal's FA Cup campaign ended after just one match, as Nottingham Forest won 1–0 at the [[City Ground]] due to an 83rd-minute goal from [[Lewis Grabban]], who finished a cross from [[Ryan Yates]]. Meanwhile, Arsenal struggled offensively all game and registered no shots on target despite dominating the time of possession. Additionally, in a rare first-half, non-injury substitution, manager Mikel Arteta sent on Kieran Tierney in place of a 'struggling' [[Nuno Tavares]] in the 35th minute.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/jan/09/nottingham-forest-arsenal-fa-cup-match-report|title=Lewis Grabban's late show for Nottingham Forest stuns Arsenal in FA Cup|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=9 January 2022|access-date=9 January 2022}}</ref> This was the first time since the [[2017–18 FA Cup|2017–18]] edition that Arsenal were knocked out in the third round, which also came at the hands of Nottingham Forest.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59911445|title=Nottingham Forest 1-0 Arsenal: Lewis Grabban knocks Gunners out of FA Cup|first=Alex|last=Bysouth|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=9 January 2022|access-date=9 January 2022}}</ref>

Four days later, Arsenal travelled to [[Anfield]] for the first leg of the EFL Cup semi-finals against Liverpool. An injury to [[Cédric Soares|Cédric]] early in the match forced a substitution in the 11th minute, with [[Calum Chambers]] replacing him at right-back. Moments later, Arsenal nearly conceded the opening goal, as [[Jordan Henderson]] charged down and blocked a long kick from Aaron Ramsdale, but the deflection went wide of the open goal and resulted in a Liverpool corner. In the 24th minute, Granit Xhaka was sent off by referee [[Michael Oliver (referee)|Michael Oliver]] for a high boot and a denial of a clear goal-scoring opportunity, as the former attempted to intercept a long pass from [[Andrew Robertson]] to [[Diogo Jota]]. The red card meant that Xhaka would miss Arsenal's next two matches. It also prompted Arteta to make another early substitution, with centre-back [[Rob Holding]] replacing striker [[Eddie Nketiah]] to provide defensive cover.
