Despite playing with only 10 players for the rest of the match, Arsenal held Liverpool to a 0–0 draw, with [[Takumi Minamino]] shooting over an open goal in the closing minutes and missing Liverpool's other best scoring chance.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/jan/13/liverpool-arsenal-carabao-cup-semi-final-first-leg-match-report|title=Arsenal dig in to deny Liverpool in first leg despite Granit Xhaka red card|first=Andy|last=Hunter|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=13 January 2022|access-date=14 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59889970|title=Liverpool 0-0 Arsenal: Hosts frustrated by 10-man Gunners in their Carabao Cup semi-final first leg|first=Harry|last=Poole|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=13 January 2022|access-date=14 January 2022}}</ref>

On 15 January, the Premier League accepted Arsenal's request to postpone the [[North London derby|match]] against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], which would have been held the following day, due to an insufficient amount of available players in the Arsenal squad as a result of COVID-19, existing and recent injuries, and players away with their countries at the Africa Cup of Nations.<ref name="nld-pp">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/north-london-derby-postponed|title=North London derby is postponed|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=15 January 2022|access-date=15 January 2022}}</ref>

On 18 January, [[Sead Kolašinac]] left the club by mutual consent and signed with [[Ligue 1]] club [[Olympique de Marseille]], joining up with Arsenal loanees [[Matteo Guendouzi]] and [[William Saliba]].<ref name="kolasinac">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/sead-kolasinac-leaves-mutual-consent-olympique-marseille|title=Sead Kolasinac leaves by mutual consent|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=18 January 2022|access-date=18 January 2022}}</ref> Two days later, [[Pablo Marí]] was loaned out to Serie A club [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]] until the end of the season.<ref name="mari">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/pablo-mari-joins-udinese-loan|title=Pablo Mari joins Udinese on loan|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=20 January 2022|access-date=20 January 2022}}</ref>

That same day, in the second leg of the EFL Cup semi-finals, Arsenal were knocked out of the competition at home 2–0 by Liverpool, thanks to a brace from Diogo Jota. Both sides came close to scoring early in the match, with Alexandre Lacazette's fifth-minute free kick hitting the crossbar and [[Joël Matip]]'s tap-in disallowed for offside minutes later, before Jota scored the opener in the 17th minute. After Liverpool came close with [[Ibrahima Konaté]]'s header from a [[Trent Alexander-Arnold]] corner hitting the post early in the second half, they finally scored a second goal as Jota received a long pass from Alexander-Arnold and chipped the ball over an onrushing Aaron Ramsdale. To make matters worse for Arsenal, 74th-minute substitute Thomas Partey, who had just returned from international duty after Ghana's early elimination from the Africa Cup of Nations, received a second yellow card for a late tackle on [[Fabinho (footballer, born 1993)|Fabinho]] and was sent off in the closing minutes of the game, having received his first yellow card for a foul on [[Neco Williams]] minutes earlier.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/jan/20/diogo-jota-double-sinks-arsenal-to-send-liverpool-through-to-carabao-cup-final|title=Diogo Jota double sinks Arsenal and sends Liverpool into Carabao Cup final|first=Jonathan|last=Liew|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=20 January 2022|access-date=21 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59824287|title=Arsenal 0-2 Liverpool (0-2 agg): Diogo Jota double sets up Chelsea final for Reds|first=Phil|last=McNulty|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=20 January 2022|access-date=21 January 2022}}</ref>

Arsenal returned to Premier League competition on 23 January at home against [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]]. However, despite Arsenal having three times as much possession as Burnley and dominating shots and corners, neither team was able to break the deadlock and the match finished 0–0, which ended Arsenal's month-long spell in fourth place and dropped them to sixth.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/jan/23/arsenal-burnley-premier-league-match-report|title=Arsenal's Alexandre Lacazette is off target as resilient Burnley hold out|first=Sam|last=Dalling|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=23 January 2022|access-date=27 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60012766|title=Arsenal 0-0 Burnley: Gunners held in Premier League stalemate|first=Joe|last=Rindl|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=23 January 2022|access-date=27 January 2022}}</ref>

The club continued their exodus of players in the winter transfer window, as [[Calum Chambers]] joined fellow Premier League club [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on a permanent transfer announced on 27 January.<ref name="chambers">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/calum-chambers-joins-aston-villa|title=Calum Chambers joins Aston Villa|first=Alex|last=Taylor|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=27 January 2022|access-date=27 January 2022}}</ref>

On the final day of that transfer window, Arsenal made their first and only first-team acquisition, signing 23-year-old American centre-back [[Auston Trusty]] from [[Major League Soccer]] club [[Colorado Rapids]], although Trusty will stay with the Rapids on loan until 17 July 2022.<ref name="trusty">{{cite web|url=https://www.coloradorapids.com/news/colorado-rapids-transfer-auston-trusty-to-arsenal-fc|title=Colorado Rapids Transfer Auston Trusty to Arsenal FC|publisher=Colorado Rapids|date=31 January 2022|access-date=31 January 2022}}</ref> The following day, it was announced that former captain Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, who had not been selected for any match squads since the loss to Everton in early December, had left the club by mutual consent,<ref name="auba-leaves">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-leaves-arsenal|title=Aubameyang leaves club by mutual consent|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=1 February 2022|access-date=1 February 2022}}</ref> with it being announced later that he had joined [[La Liga]] club [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref name="auba-barca">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2467985/fc-barcelona-sign-pierre-emerick-aubameyang|title=FC Barcelona sign Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang|publisher=F.C. Barcelona|date=2 February 2022|access-date=2 February 2022}}</ref>

=== February ===
After the international break, Arsenal travelled to [[Molineux Stadium|Molineux]] to face [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] on 10 February. In the 25th minute, after a half-clearance from a Gabriel Martinelli corner, both Alexandre Lacazette and [[José Sá]] went for the ball and missed, with Gabriel scoring the tap-in for the game's only goal. In the 69th minute, referee [[Michael Oliver (referee)|Michael Oliver]] showed Martinelli two yellow cards in quick succession, amounting to a red card and dismissal; the first was for shoving [[Daniel Podence]] and preventing a quick throw-in, and the second was for chasing him down and fouling him again. Despite being reduced to 10 players, Arsenal maintained their lead and won 1–0.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/feb/10/wolves-arsenal-premier-league-match-report|title=Gabriel bundles Arsenal past Wolves despite Martinelli's remarkable red card|first=Ben|last=Fisher|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=10 February 2022|access-date=25 February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60239159|title=Wolverhampton Wanderers 0-1 Arsenal: Gabriel scores only goal at Molineux|first=Emlyn|last=Begley|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=10 February 2022|access-date=25 February 2022}}</ref>

On 19 February, Arsenal hosted Brentford, to whom they had lost the season opener. Neither club scored in the first half, but three minutes into the second half, Emile Smith Rowe broke the deadlock with his low curling shot past [[David Raya]]. In the 79th minute, Arsenal were on the break, and Bukayo Saka finished off a pass from Thomas Partey with a curling strike that ricocheted in off the far post. However, Brentford scoring a consolation goal in stoppage time, with a scramble in the box following a [[Saman Ghoddos]] free kick resulting in Christian Norgaard's close-range strike, which was confirmed after a VAR check for offside. There was not enough time for Brentford to seek an equalising goal, so Arsenal won 2–1.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/feb/19/arsenal-brentford-premier-league-match-report|title=Saka seals comfortable victory over Brentford for assured Arsenal|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=19 February 2022|access-date=25 February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60239159|title=Arsenal 2-1 Brentford: Smith Rowe and Saka on target as Gunners close in on top four|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=19 February 2022|access-date=25 February 2022}}</ref>

Arsenal continued to make up their games in hand and played the reverse fixture against Wolverhampton Wanderers at home on 25 February; the match had originally been scheduled for 28 December 2021 but was postponed due to a lack of available players in the Wolves squad as a result of numerous injuries and positive [[COVID-19]] test results.<ref name="wolves-ppd">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59797714|title=Arsenal v Wolves game postponed because of Covid-19|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=26 December 2021|access-date=26 December 2021}}</ref> Wolves scored first, with [[Hwang Hee-chan]] intercepting a back pass from Gabriel to Aaron Ramsdale and scoring in the 10th minute. They maintained their lead for most of the match, until Arsenal equalised in the 82nd minute. Substitute Eddie Nketiah received Martin Ødegaard's lofted pass and cut it back for fellow substitute Nicolas Pépé, who spun around and scored with his stronger left foot. Five minutes into stoppage time, Alexandre Lacazette received a pass from Pépé and shot towards goal, with the strike being diverted into the top corner off José Sá's glove, giving Arsenal another 2–1 win.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/feb/24/arsenal-wolves-premier-league-match-report|title=Lacazette forces late Arsenal winner to complete comeback against Wolves|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=24 February 2022|access-date=25 February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59736889|title=Arsenal 2-1 Wolverhampton Wanderers: Late own goal from visiting goalkeeper Jose Sa gives hosts dramatic win|first=Steve|last=Sutcliffe|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=24 February 2022|access-date=25 February 2022}}</ref>

=== March ===
Arsenal went to [[Vicarage Road]] on 6 March to face [[Watford F.C.|Watford]]. Less than 20 seconds into the match, [[Emmanuel Dennis]] scored but the goal was ruled offside. In the fifth minute, Martin Ødegaard slotted the ball past [[Ben Foster (footballer)|Ben Foster]] after receiving a pass from Bukayo Saka. Watford levelled the score six minutes later with a bicycle kick from [[Cucho Hernández]]. At the half-hour mark, Alexandre Lacazette returned a pass to Saka, who struck into the top corner. In the 52nd minute, Lacazette provided another assist, setting the ball for Gabriel Martinelli's strike. A late goal from [[Moussa Sissoko]] reduced Watford's deficit, but Arsenal held on for a 3–2 victory and moved back into the top four.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/mar/06/watford-arsenal-premier-league-match-report|title=Gabriel Martinelli sends Arsenal fourth despite Watford fightback|first=Nick|last=Ames|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=6 March 2022|access-date=6 March 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60531485|title=Watford 2-3 Arsenal: Three classy goals take Gunners into fourth place|first=Emlyn|last=Begley|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=6 March 2022|access-date=6 March 2022}}</ref>
 
On 14 March, Arsenal faced Leicester City at home. The Gunners opened the scoring just after the tenth minute. A corner by Gabriel Martinelli was met by the head of Thomas Partey at the near-post. Partey could have had a brace just seven minutes later, when a deflected shot by Granit Xhaka dropped to the Ghanaian, who saw his shot from the edge of the box rattle off the Leicester upright. Leicester nearly found an equaliser in the 34th minute, when a cross by [[Marc Albrighton]] was headed towards goal by Barnes. The header from just outside the six-yard box was met by a strong right palm from goalkeeper Aaron Ramsdale. In the 54th minute, Arsenal had a penalty shout when Thomas Partey's header was glanced by the hand of defender [[Çağlar Söyüncü]]. After a lengthy VAR check, referee Anthony Taylor awarded the Gunners a penalty. The resulting spot-kick was converted by Alexandre Lacazette. Thereby doubling Arsenal's lead in the 59th minute and also marking Alexandre Lacazette's 200th senior career goal. The result brought Arsenal back into fourth, leapfrogging Manchester United.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/12562548/arsenal-2-0-leicester-thomas-partey-and-alexandre-lacazette-score-as-gunners-move-back-up-to-fourth|title=Arsenal 2-0 Leicester: Thomas Partey and Alexandre Lacazette score as Gunners move back up to fourth|first=Adam|last=Bate|work=[[Sky Sports]]|date=14 March 2022|access-date=14 March 2022}}</ref>

Arsenal welcomed Liverpool to the Emirates Stadium on 17 March. The Gunner's fought valiantly in the first half, limiting Liverpool's dominant attacking players to speculative half-chances. However, failing to capitalize on their own chances. The momentum swung Liverpool's way in the second-half, with [[Sadio Mané]] netting a goal which was immediately chalked off for offside within two minutes of the half. Arsenal could have broken the deadlock themselves, when Martin Ødegaard's shot was saved by goalkeeper [[Alisson Becker|Alisson]] following a misplaced back-pass by [[Thiago Alcântara|Thiago]]. The opener was finally scored by [[Diogo Jota]] in the 54th minute, with his shot beating Aaron Ramsdale at the near-post following a through-ball by Thiago. Liverpool would go on to double their lead eight minutes later, when [[Roberto Firmino]] tapped-in from close range via a cross by [[Andrew Robertson]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/20876/12566916/arsenal-0-2-liverpool-diogo-jota-and-roberto-firmino-fire-reds-to-within-one-point-of-leaders-man-city|title=Arsenal 0-2 Liverpool: Diogo Jota and Roberto Firmino fire Reds to within one point of leaders Man City|first=Adam|last=Bate|work=[[Sky Sports]]|date=17 March 2022|access-date=17 March 2022}}</ref>

=== April ===
Arsenal kicked off the month of April with an away trip to [[Selhurst Park]] to face [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] on 4 April. Goals from [[Jean-Philippe Mateta]] and [[Jordan Ayew]] before half-time followed by a [[Wilfried Zaha]] penalty condemned Arsenal to a 3–0 defeat.<ref>{{Cite web |title=04/04/2022 - Crystal Palace - Premier League - Men - A |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Apr-04/crystal-palace |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=Match build up and reaction from Crystal Palace V Arsenal {{!}} Arsenal.com |language=en}}</ref> Next, Arsenal hosted Brighton on 9 April. Brighton ended up with a two-goal lead thanks to goals from [[Leandro Trossard]] and [[Enock Mwepu]]. An 89th-minute goal from Martin Ødegaard came too late, as Arsenal ended up losing 1–2 to the visitors.<ref>{{Cite web |title=09/04/2022 - Brighton - Premier League - Men - H |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Apr-09/brighton |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=Match build up and reaction from Arsenal V Brighton {{!}} Arsenal.com |language=en}}</ref> Arsenal's losing streak increased to three consecutive matches after losing 1–0 to [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] at [[St Mary's Stadium]] on 16 April, with the contest's sole goal coming from [[Jan Bednarek]] in the 44th minute.<ref>{{Cite web |title=16/04/2022 - Southampton - Premier League - Men - A |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Apr-16/southampton |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=Match build up and reaction from Southampton V Arsenal {{!}} Arsenal.com |language=en}}</ref> Arsenal finally ended their losing streak on 20 April with a 4–2 away win at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]; Arsenal's goals came via a brace from Eddie Nketiah, and one each from Emile Smith Rowe and Bukayo Saka.<ref>{{Cite web |title=20/04/2022 - Chelsea - Premier League - Men - A |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Apr-20/chelsea |access-date=2022-11-02 |website=Match build up and reaction from Chelsea V Arsenal {{!}} Arsenal.com |language=en}}</ref> Arsenal finished off the month by facing [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at home on 23 April. An early goal from Tavares and a 31st-minute penalty conversion by Saka gave Arsenal a quick two goal lead, before [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] put United back in the game in the 34th minute. Granit Xhaka scored in the 70th minute to seal a 3–1 win for Arsenal to end April with back-to-back victories.<ref>{{Cite web |title=23/04/2022 - Manchester United - Premier League - Men - H |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Apr-23/manchester-united |access-date=2022-11-02 |website=Match build up and reaction from Arsenal V Manchester United {{!}} Arsenal.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== May ===
Arsenal started the final month of the season traveling to the [[London Stadium]] to face [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] on 1 May. Rob Holding and Gabriel scored for Arsenal either side of a West Ham equaliser from [[Jarrod Bowen]] to secure a 2–1 victory for the Gunners, which extended their win streak to three.<ref>{{Cite web |title=01/05/2022 - West Ham United - Premier League - Men - A |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-May-01/west-ham-united |access-date=2022-11-02 |website=Match build up and reaction from West Ham United V Arsenal {{!}} Arsenal.com |language=en}}</ref> Next, Arsenal hosted [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] on 8 May. Eddie Nketiah scored a brace within 10 minutes, and despite a 66th-minute goal from [[Diego Llorente]], Arsenal held on for a 2–1 win, extending their win streak to four matches. Arsenal then faced [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Spurs]] at the [[Tottenham Hotspur Stadium]] on 12 May. Arsenal's winning streak was snapped, as a brace from [[Harry Kane]] and a goal from [[Son Heung-min]] gave Tottenham a 3–0 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=12/05/2022 - Tottenham Hotspur - Premier League - Men - A |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-May-12/tottenham-hotspur |access-date=2022-11-02 |website=Match build up and reaction from Tottenham Hotspur V Arsenal {{!}} Arsenal.com |language=en}}</ref> Hoping to bounce back, Arsenal visited [[St James' Park]] on 16 May to face [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]. Both of the match's goals would come in the second half, as a 56th-minute opener from [[Callum Wilson (footballer, born 1992)|Callum Wilson]] followed by an 85th-minute strike by [[Bruno Guimarães]] gave Newcastle a 2–0 victory and saw Arsenal fall below Tottenham in the table on the penultimate matchday.<ref>{{Cite web |title=16/05/2022 - Newcastle United - Premier League - Men - H |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-May-16/newcastle-united#!match-news |access-date=2022-11-02 |website=Match build up and reaction from Arsenal V Newcastle United {{!}} Arsenal.com |language=en}}</ref> Arsenal's final match of the season was at home against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]]. Going into the match, Arsenal not only had to win, but Spurs also had to lose for Arsenal to qualify for next season's [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]]. Arsenal beat Everton in a 5–1 rout, but due to Spurs also winning their match, the Gunners qualified for the [[2022–23 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] instead, finishing the season in fifth place with 69 points.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Match report: Arsenal 5-1 Everton |url=https://www.arsenal.com/premier-league-match-report-everton-mikel-arteta-emirates-stadium |access-date=2022-11-02 |website=Match report: Arsenal 5-1 Everton |date=22 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

== Friendlies ==
On 16 April 2021, Arsenal announced that they would participate in a pre-season fixture against defending [[Scottish Professional Football League]] champions [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on 17 July at the [[Ibrox Stadium]], in order to celebrate Rangers' 150th anniversary.<ref name="es">{{cite news|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/arsenal-rangers-summer-preseason-friendly-b930100.html|title=Arsenal to play Rangers in pre-season friendly as Scottish champions mark 150th anniversary|first=Simon|last=Collings|newspaper=[[Evening Standard]]|date=16 April 2021|access-date=18 April 2021}}</ref> This forms part of a training camp in Scotland, with another friendly being played against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] four days earlier.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-set-up-pre-season-friendly-against-arsenal-3240443|title=Hibs set up pre-season friendly against Arsenal|first=Patrick|last=McPartlin|newspaper=[[Edinburgh Evening News]]|date=18 May 2021|access-date=18 May 2021}}</ref>

=== Florida Cup ===
Arsenal confirmed they will travel to the [[United States]] to compete in the seventh edition of the [[Florida Cup (soccer)|Florida Cup]] in [[Orlando, Florida]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-compete-florida-cup-july|title=Arsenal to compete in Florida Cup in July|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=2 June 2021|access-date=2 June 2021}}</ref> On July 20, Arsenal withdrew from the Cup, citing "a small number of positive [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports|COVID]] tests."<ref name="FloridaCupWithdrawal"/>

== Awards ==
Each club Player of the Month and Goal of the Month award winner was chosen via [[open-access poll]]s on the club's official website. While the Player of the Month awards only include the men's senior team, the Goal of the Month awards include contenders from both the men's and women's teams.
